About Me

I am a second-year PhD student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC), advised by Professor Minh N. Do. I am also fortunate to work closely with Professor Ge Liu. Before joining UIUC, I received my B.Sc. in Mathematics from the University of Hong Kong.

Research Interests


My research lies at the intersection of Multimodal Representation Learning, Generative Modeling, Robotics, and AI for Healthcare and Biomedicine.


I aim to build theoretically grounded and scalable learning frameworks for multimodal intelligence. In multimodal representation learning, I explore new perspectives and principled objectives that capture structure both across and within modalities. In generative modeling, I focus on making generation both efficient and controllable.


More broadly, I view representation and generation as complementary facets of intelligence, and I seek unified learning paradigms in which each informs the other across modalities. I am particularly interested in how the capacities to perceive, understand, reason, predict, generate, and act can develop together and reinforce one another—giving rise to systems that learn from their own experience and continually improve through interaction with the world.
